claims.statement: For the r-bit indicator q_r which vanishes at exactly one point, Phi(q_r)/I(q_r)=2(2^r-1)/r times [r-(2^r-2)2^{-r} log2(2^r-1)]; this ratio is strictly greater than 4 for every r>=3, approaches 4 from above, and is preserved by every tensor power.
claims.scope: Every integer r>=3 and every positive tensor depth k; exact disjoint-product indicator family in dimension rk.

claims.statement: The universal unsigned estimate Phi(q)<=4 I(q) fails already for the three-bit co-singleton indicator, where Phi/I=14-(7/2)log2(7)>4.
claims.scope: Exact Boolean indicator witness; strict sign certified by 7^7<2^20 and amplified to every tensor depth.

claims.statement: The six-bit indicator mask 18446708751093190623 and all its tensor powers satisfy Phi/I=K*=4.512256384896659..., forcing K>=K*>4.5 in every universal estimate Phi(q)<=K I(q).
claims.scope: Exact seed and every positive tensor power; rational lower bound certified by 2^3024>3^547*19^475*7^49.

claims.statement: For f_k=2q^{tensor k}-1, the co-singleton r=3 family and the six-bit seed family have bounded genuine-Boolean FEI ratios, with limits 5.073268136529566... and 5.244969399712791... respectively.
claims.scope: All positive tensor depths, with exact closed formulas and asymptotic limits; these are controls, not FEI counterfamilies.

claims.statement: The complete finite sign ensemble is paid, but the actual physical signing still lacks a uniform activation witness. Independent unsigned coefficient-four payments of the activation indicators are now refuted; a joint signed near/separated, posterior-activation, or terminal-reserve mechanism remains necessary.
